options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questionText:
Read the following algorithmic sorting case study and answer the questions that follow:

A triage nurse in a hospital emergency department records patient priority triage codes (values from 1 to 5, where 1 is critical). To organize incoming patient files in memory, a software engineer implements two classic sorting algorithms: Bubble Sort and Insertion Sort. In Bubble Sort, adjacent elements are compared and swapped if they are in the wrong order. With each complete pass, the largest remaining element bubbles up to its final position at the end of the array. For an array of n elements, Bubble Sort requires at most n - 1 passes. In Insertion Sort, the array is conceptually partitioned into a sorted sublist and an unsorted sublist. Elements from the unsorted sublist are picked one by one and inserted into their correct relative position within the sorted sublist by shifting greater elements to the right.

Question: How does Insertion Sort integrate an element from the unsorted sublist into the sorted sublist?

options.text: By swapping with the last element of the list
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option 'By swapping with the last element of the list'. Conflates core domain concepts or theories with adjacent terminology.

options.text: By shifting elements greater than the key to the right and inserting the key into its correct vacant spot
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately analyzes case evidence on Insertion Sort Operation.
Incorrect option 'By deleting all duplicates'. Attributes historical facts, dates, authors, or mechanisms to an incorrect entity.
Incorrect option 'By reversing the sorted sublist'. Adopts an over-generalized or inaccurate interpretation contradictory to syllabus facts.

detailedSolution:
Insertion Sort shifts greater elements in the sorted portion one position to the right to make room for the current key.
Hence, Option B is correct.

solution.quick: Correct answer is By shifting elements greater than the key to the right and inserting the key into its correct vacant spot.
solution.concept:
Insertion Sort shifts greater elements in the sorted portion one position to the right to make room for the current key.
Hence, Option B is correct.
solution.detailed:

A triage nurse in a hospital emergency department records patient priority triage codes (values from 1 to 5, where 1 is critical). To organize incoming patient files in memory, a software engineer implements two classic sorting algorithms: Bubble Sort and Insertion Sort. In Bubble Sort, adjacent elements are compared and swapped if they are in the wrong order. With each complete pass, the largest remaining element bubbles up to its final position at the end of the array. For an array of n elements, Bubble Sort requires at most n - 1 passes. In Insertion Sort, the array is conceptually partitioned into a sorted sublist and an unsorted sublist.
